about: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next EXL3 3.05bpw_h5_ng5 on one Arc Pro B70: experts in USM host RAM behind a device expert cache, n-gram table on NVMe (trellis-serve ft-xpu-vision 72fd2d4, text + images)
setup: NEEDS: 1x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB (the server takes the whole card: 31.85 GiB resident at peak; 9,000 expert slots = 15.61 GiB); 68 GB of free system RAM (measured peak 67.26 GB at load, 64.93 GB steady: 45.8 GB routed experts + 8 GB n-gram row cache in USM host memory + ~10.6 GB process RSS); 85.14 GB for the weights on a LOCAL NVMe SSD (the 32.6 GB n-gram table is random-read with O_DIRECT while serving). Text and images (256x256 to 4096x4096 tested; EXL3 ViT on XPU kernels). Serves ONE request at a time: concurrent requests queue (C2-C4 aggregate stays ~32.6 tok/s). Launch = trellis-serve xpu/scripts/serve_flashnext_b70.sh at 72fd2d4 with the XVIS20 settings plus --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder (not in the measured runs), on a bridge network with --shm-size 64g where the measured runs used --network host --ipc=host. Protocol sweep XVIS20 (B70 #0, omarchy): prefill 8k 1,026.6 / 16k 945.4 / 32k 798.1 / 64k 600.3 tok/s; decode C1 32.52 tok/s (C2 32.61 / C3 32.60 / C4 32.66 aggregate), C1 at 32k context 31.85. Quality vs stock exllamav3: text panel top-1 0.9893 / KL 0.00121; vision gate top-1 0.9761 / KL 0.0085, 8/8 answers correct. Context 262,144, KV pool 270,336 tokens fp8.
